title: 00 — Polars in Practice: Index
html:
00 — Polars in Practice: Index

The one idea: Polars is fast because you describe what you want as expressions and let a multithreaded, columnar engine decide how. Everything in this set is about keeping it that way: lazy queries that read only what they need, data types that fit, every core busy, memory bounded, and clean hand-offs to the files people actually use, Excel included.

1. What this set is

A hands-on companion to Polars Deep Dive, which explains the mental model, Parquet layout and the cookbook. This set goes further on the practical questions:

  • how much faster than plain Python and pandas it is, and when it isn't;
  • how the lazy engine and the Polars 2 streaming default behave;
  • how to control memory (types, streaming, sinks, spilling to disk);
  • how to control cores and run work concurrently without fighting the engine;
  • how to create test data;
  • how to read and write Excel, and fill a designer's Excel template with data.

Every example was run on Polars 2.1.0 (Python 3.13, 4 vCPU, 16 GB RAM) on 2026-11-07, and its output is pasted underneath. Timings are from that machine. Yours will differ, but the ratios hold.

2. Chapter map

# Chapter What you get from it
01 Why Polars Is Fast Plain Python vs pandas vs Polars on the same job, and why map_elements is the slowest of all
02 Lazy Queries and the Optimiser scan_*, pushdown measured, reading plans, collect_all, the Polars 2 streaming default and row order
03 Memory Management Column sizes by type, Enum vs Categorical, eager vs lazy peak memory, sinks, spilling to disk
04 Cores, Threads and Concurrency POLARS_MAX_THREADS, scaling measured, collect_async, processes with spawn, oversubscription, reproducible sums
05 Creating Data Strict parsing, a silent-null trap, seeded synthetic data at scale, nested columns
06 Excel: Read and Write Formatted multi-sheet workbooks with write_excel, formulas, totals, fast reads with calamine
07 Excel Templates Fill a designed template's table from a DataFrame and keep its styles, formulas and named cells
08 Production Patterns Partitioned output, schema contracts, batched hand-off, tests, upgrading to Polars 2, a review checklist

3. Where it connects

Topic Note
Polars mental model, Parquet internals, cookbook Polars Deep Dive
Python memory, the GIL, packaging Python & Data Engineering
Threads, processes and async in general Concurrency, Async & Parallelism
Polars beside DuckDB, Daft and PyIceberg Open Lakehouse: single-node engines

4. Setup

python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install polars pyarrow fastexcel xlsxwriter openpyxl pandas numpy
python -c "import polars as pl; print(pl.__version__, pl.thread_pool_size())"

fastexcel reads Excel, xlsxwriter writes new workbooks, and openpyxl edits existing ones (templates). pandas is only needed for the comparison in chapter 01.
